stories.headline: Apple set to unveil Gemini-powered Siri reboot at WWDC after secret AI strategy meeting

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reported on June 7 that Apple's top executives, excluding Tim Cook, held a secret meeting in early 2025 to discuss how far behind it was in AI and chart a path forward — the results of which will be unveiled at WWDC on June 8.

Apple is expected to rebuild Siri on a custom Google Gemini model under a multi-year partnership reportedly worth roughly $1 billion a year, arriving two years late after Apple settled a $250 million false-advertising lawsuit over the original 2024 promises.

iOS 27 will introduce a new Extensions framework that lets any AI chatbot installed from the App Store plug into Siri, Writing Tools and Image Playground — fine print in a pre-release build reads: 'Extensions allow agents from installed apps to work with Siri, the Siri app and other features on your devices.'

Siri will live within the iPhone's Dynamic Island as a glowing animation that expands into a translucent results card, with a standalone Siri app providing persistent conversation history, file uploads, and text-and-voice modes.

Apple Intelligence will expand into the Camera app with a Visual Intelligence mode powered by Google Image Search, and the Photos app is expected to gain AI editing tools including scene extension, object removal and natural-language edits.

stories.headline: Memory vendors say China's CXMT DDR5 is no bargain — prices match Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron

key_facts.fact: Memory module vendors at Computex 2026 told Wccftech that CXMT's DDR5 prices are 'almost on par' with Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron, debunking the assumption that the Chinese newcomer would crash consumer pricing
CXMT's edge comes from supply, not price: since it does not prioritize HBM or SOCAMM for AI customers it has more traditional DRAM capacity available for client markets

CXMT also does not impose the supply penalties that Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron currently force on customers seeking additional allocation — making it an attractive secondary source despite matching prices
A Lexar regional manager warned at Computex that DRAM prices could double by year-end, with current channel discounts merely reflecting short-term inventory clearance

stories.headline: UK, France, Germany back direct Zelensky-Putin ceasefire talks; Zelensky open to freezing front lines

key_facts.fact: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer, French President Emmanuel Macron and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky at 10 Downing Street on Sunday June 7 and issued a joint statement supporting direct dialogue between Ukraine and Russia, with active US and European participation, to bring about a ceasefire.

In a Sky News interview, Zelensky said he would accept freezing the war along current front lines as the 'quickest way' to halt the fighting, while stressing it must lead to broader diplomatic talks to prevent renewed aggression.

The leaders set five conditions for a 'just and lasting peace', starting with an immediate and complete ceasefire, the current line of contact as the starting point for talks, legally binding security guarantees for Ukraine including a multinational force, and keeping Russian assets frozen until Russia compensates Ukraine.

Putin rebuffed Zelensky's open-letter proposal for face-to-face talks, saying he saw 'no point' in such a meeting until a peace deal was agreed and insisting that any settlement would require Ukraine to surrender the entire Donetsk region.
Zelensky also told Starmer that Ukraine needed more missiles for air defence systems as Russia's war stretched into its fifth year, with daily strikes on Ukrainian energy and civilian infrastructure.

stories.headline: Factorial raises $150M Series D at $2.5B valuation for AI 'workforce operations' platform

key_facts.fact: Spanish-founded Factorial closed a $150 million Series D at a $2.5 billion valuation on June 8, led by General Catalyst in its first direct equity investment in the company, with Atomico and Four Rivers joining.

Alongside the equity round, General Catalyst is committing up to an additional $540 million through its Customer Value Fund, bringing total capital committed to more than $700 million, with returns tied to and capped by customer value created.

Factorial has rebuilt its product around a two-agent model in Factorial One: one agent represents the organization and applies company policies across HR, finance and IT, while the other represents the individual employee and executes tasks on their behalf.
Factorial serves more than 16,000 businesses across more than 90 countries and is pitching its 'fewer agents, clearer accountability' thesis against rivals deploying hundreds of specialized agents.

stories.headline: Iran fires missiles at Israel after Beirut strike; Israel hits Iranian petrochemical and military sites

key_facts.fact: Iran launched ballistic missiles at Israel on Sunday evening June 7, the first such attack since the April 8 ceasefire took effect, after Israel struck Beirut's southern Dahiyeh suburb earlier in the day.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps targeted Israel's Ramat David airbase with ballistic missiles, calling the strike a response to Israeli attacks on Hezbollah in Beirut. The IRGC said the Israeli aircraft that struck Hezbollah sites flew from Ramat David.
Israel retaliated overnight Monday June 8 with strikes on Iranian military targets and a petrochemical complex in the Mahshahr area in southwest Iran, with Iranian reports saying 15 targets were hit.

President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social at 5:36am ET pleading 'Israel and Iran must immediately stop "shooting."' Iran's foreign ministry then blamed the US for the resumption of conflict, calling Washington an 'arsonist.'
Iran fired 30 ballistic missiles in total at Israel according to an Israeli military official, and Yemen's Houthi rebels also fired a missile at Tel Aviv that was intercepted.
Israel closed all crossings into Gaza, including Kerem Shalom and Rafah, after Iran's missile attack. Iraq's Civil Aviation Authority closed national airspace for 72 hours and Syria for 12 hours.

The Israeli strike on Beirut's southern suburbs that triggered the chain reaction killed at least two people and wounded around 20, hitting an area that had become sensitive in ceasefire negotiations days after Israel and Lebanon agreed to a US-hosted ceasefire that Hezbollah rejected.

stories.headline: Meta confirms over 20,000 Instagram accounts hijacked via AI chatbot password reset bug

key_facts.fact: Meta confirmed in a notice to Maine's attorney general that 20,225 Instagram accounts were hijacked after attackers exploited a vulnerability in its AI-assisted account recovery tool, with the campaign beginning April 17.

The bug was in Meta's High Touch Support tool: when an attacker provided an email address not previously associated with the target Instagram account, the system incorrectly sent a password reset link to that unassociated email instead of rejecting the request.
Once attackers reset the password, they were able to log into any account that did not have two-factor authentication enabled, gaining access to DMs, profile data and posts.

Meta discovered the vulnerability on May 31, has disabled the abused tool, invalidated the exploited reset links and enrolled affected accounts in a mandatory security checkpoint with password resets.
Meta said it is reviewing other chatbots across its platforms for similar flaws and is checking whether the same issue exists elsewhere.

stories.headline: Moonshot AI in talks for $30B valuation, a sevenfold jump in six months for China's Kimi maker

key_facts.fact: Beijing-based Moonshot AI is seeking to raise between $1 billion and $2 billion at a valuation of up to $30 billion, according to a person familiar with the matter cited by Bloomberg on June 8.

The targeted valuation is roughly 50% higher than the $20 billion it achieved in a Meituan-led round completed in May, and represents a sevenfold jump from the $4 billion valuation Moonshot held in December 2025.
The new round is Moonshot's third financing in six months and would bring total fundraising over that period to roughly $3.9 billion.
Moonshot's annual recurring revenue topped $200 million in April, implying a price-to-sales ratio of about 150x at the $30 billion target.

A $30 billion mark would place Moonshot ahead of publicly listed peer MiniMax (around $20 billion) but still behind Zhipu AI (about $80 billion) and DeepSeek, which is reportedly pursuing roughly $50-59 billion in its first major round.

stories.headline: Naver and Nvidia team up to build gigawatt-scale AI factory, starting at 55MW in 2027

key_facts.fact: Nvidia and Naver announced on June 7, 2026 that Naver will expand sovereign AI infrastructure starting at 55 megawatts with plans to move to gigawatt scale using the Nvidia DSX platform
The new DSX-powered cloud will expand Naver's Gak Sejong data center in Sejong, South Korea, which will serve as a forward base
Naver plans to begin with 55MW operation in the first half of 2027, expand overseas infrastructure to 100MW within the same year, and to 200MW by 2028
One gigawatt is roughly four times the maximum capacity of Naver's largest domestic data center, Gak Sejong, and can accommodate hundreds of thousands of Nvidia's latest GPUs simultaneously
Naver Chairman Lee Hae-jin and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang met at Naver's 1784 headquarters in Seongnam to discuss a roadmap to expand into Europe and the Middle East beyond Asia-Pacific

stories.headline: Doosan opens Nvidia partnership to SMRs, gas turbines and an Agentic Robot OS

key_facts.fact: Doosan Group said on June 8, 2026 that four affiliates — Doosan Robotics, Doosan Bobcat, Doosan Enerbility and Doosan Corporation Electro-Materials BG — will expand cooperation with Nvidia across physical AI, robotics and AI factory infrastructure
Doosan Enerbility is exploring how its gas turbines, steam turbines and small modular reactors plus Doosan Fuel Cell's hydrogen fuel-cell systems can support Nvidia's DSX AI factory platform

Doosan Robotics is integrating Nvidia Isaac Sim, Isaac Lab, the Cosmos world foundation models, Newton physics engine and Jetson Thor into its Agentic Robot OS — an AI platform connecting perception, reasoning, simulation, learning and on-device inference
Doosan Robotics also plans to develop reference use cases for industrial tasks such as pallet sorting and polishing and to extend to dual-arm and humanoid form factors

Huang said combining Nvidia DSX and physical AI with Doosan's energy, robotics and advanced materials businesses can secure new growth engines in intelligent robots, autonomous industrial equipment and next-generation infrastructure

stories.headline: Hyundai pitches Nvidia on $5.9B Saemangeum AI valley while expanding mobility and robotics ties

key_facts.fact: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang met Hyundai Motor Group Executive Chair Euisun Chung on June 8, 2026 at the automaker's headquarters in Seoul to discuss expanding partnership across mobility, robotics and AI factories

Chung briefed Huang on a 9 trillion-won (US$5.87 billion) project announced in February to transform 1.12 million square meters of the Saemangeum reclaimed land area into an AI, robotics and hydrogen hub

Huang said 'the next wave of AI is mobility and physical AI. This is the future where AI understands the world and can come out and do good work, productive work for the world. This is the time for Hyundai'
The two companies are jointly investing roughly $3 billion to establish an Nvidia AI Technology Center and a Hyundai Motor Group Physical AI Application Center in Korea
Hyundai previously unveiled plans to build an AI factory powered by 50,000 Nvidia Blackwell GPUs for in-vehicle AI, autonomous driving, smart manufacturing and robotics

stories.headline: LG expands Nvidia pact to cover physical AI, cooling and 800V DC power for AI data centers

key_facts.fact: LG Group Chairman Koo Kwang-mo and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang met on June 8, 2026 at LG Twin Towers in Yeouido, Seoul to expand strategic cooperation across physical AI, AI data centers and mobility

LG Electronics will pursue certification cooperation on Coolant Distribution Units (CDU) and cold plates for AI data centers, plus modular data center design based on Nvidia's Digital Twin Supercomputing Matrix (DSX)
LG Energy Solution is discussing an 800V direct current-based power solution and Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) cooperation with Nvidia to handle AI data centers' rising power demand
Huang said today's data centers already reach hundreds of megawatts and future ultra-large blocks will require advanced cooling and power supply technologies where LG has 'fantastic capabilities'
LG Uplus will build a large AI data center using Nvidia GPUs and LG CNS is developing scalable AI factory infrastructure using Nvidia's reference architecture

stories.headline: Nvidia and SK Hynix sign multi-year pact for next-gen memory across Vera Rubin and Jetson Thor

key_facts.fact: Nvidia and SK Hynix announced on June 7, 2026 a multi-year technology partnership to advance next-generation memory for the global AI factory buildout and accelerate semiconductor design and manufacturing
SK Hynix will co-develop memory for Nvidia Vera Rubin AI supercomputers, Vera CPUs, RTX Spark-powered PCs and Jetson Thor robotic computing platforms
Industry analysts estimate SK Hynix holds roughly 60% to 70% of HBM4 volume allocated to Vera Rubin, with Samsung at approximately 25% to 30% and Micron supplying the remainder
Jensen Huang said 'AI factories are the engines of the next industrial revolution, and advanced memory is essential to their performance'

SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won said SK Hynix and Nvidia 'have laid the groundwork for this over several years, and this partnership is the result that shows the depth of cooperation between the two companies'

stories.headline: Nvidia signs multi-year AI pacts with SK Hynix, Naver, SK Telecom and Doosan in South Korea

key_facts.fact: Nvidia and SK Hynix announced a multi-year technology partnership on June 7-8 to co-develop next-generation memory for Vera Rubin AI supercomputers, Vera CPUs, RTX Spark-powered PCs and Jetson Thor robotic computing platforms.

Jensen Huang told reporters at SK Group headquarters in Seoul that SK Hynix would remain Nvidia's largest memory partner, and confirmed the agreement runs more than two years with an option to extend.

Naver will build AI factories on Nvidia's DSX platform at its GAK Sejong data center, starting with 55 megawatts in the first half of 2027 and scaling toward gigawatt-class capacity capable of housing hundreds of thousands of Nvidia GPUs.

SK Telecom will build a gigawatt-scale AI cloud in South Korea using Nvidia's DSX platform, with the first AI data center to come online in 2027, powered by Nvidia Blackwell GPUs and the Vera Rubin supercomputer.

Nvidia also announced that conglomerate Doosan will use its technology for robotics, and South Korea's tech ministry said it plans to secure 9,704 GPUs for a state AI project worth 2.08 trillion won in 2026, including 2,016 Vera Rubin GPUs.

Naver will also join Nvidia's Nemotron Coalition to advance its proprietary HyperCLOVA X large language model, and will develop a 'Seoul World Model' combining street-view data with Nvidia's Cosmos world foundation models for physical AI.

stories.headline: Brent jumps near $97 as Iran-Israel strikes resume and Hormuz remains closed

key_facts.fact: Brent crude futures for July advanced 4.35% to $97.14 per barrel and WTI futures for August jumped 4.25% to $94.39 on Monday June 8 after Iran and Israel traded strikes for the first time since the April ceasefire.

Before the war began in late February, Brent traded near $72 a barrel, and on Friday June 5 prices had fallen to around $93 as traders gained confidence that renewed conflict with Iran was growing less likely.

Israel said on Monday it had struck a petrochemical facility in southwestern Iran along with military targets, despite reports that Trump had urged Netanyahu to avoid further military action, dashing hopes that crude shipments through the Strait of Hormuz might resume.
Analysts said the OPEC+ output increase is unlikely to fully offset market concerns because many OPEC+ producers remain unable to achieve their production targets due to the Hormuz blockade.
Oilprice.com reported the surge live on June 7, with Brent climbing 3.45% to $96.30 and WTI 3.41% to $93.63 shortly after the Iranian launches, before further gains as Israel retaliated.

stories.headline: OPEC+ approves fourth straight output quota hike of 188,000 bpd from July

key_facts.fact: Seven core OPEC+ members decided on Sunday June 7 to increase output targets by 188,000 barrels per day from July, the fourth such hike since the Strait of Hormuz closure.
The July hike matches the June increase, which was lowered from monthly increases of 206,000 bpd in May and April after the United Arab Emirates exited OPEC after almost 60 years.

From April to June the seven core members have raised quotas by almost 600,000 bpd, even though several producers including Saudi Arabia have been unable to supply customers in full since the end of February because of the Hormuz disruption.

A separate Sunday meeting of all OPEC+ members made no change to the group-wide output policy that runs through the end of 2026, and the group affirmed it would complete a capacity review for use as the 2027 production baselines.
OPEC published the decision under the headline 'Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria, and Oman adjust production and reaffirm commitment to market stability' on 7 June 2026.

stories.headline: OpenAI plans biggest ChatGPT overhaul into 'superapp' with Codex and AI agents ahead of IPO

key_facts.fact: The Financial Times reported on June 7 that OpenAI is planning its biggest ChatGPT overhaul yet, turning it into a 'superapp' with coding tools and AI agents, set to roll out in the coming weeks via updates to the website and mobile apps.
An unnamed senior OpenAI employee told the FT that 'Chat is dead,' framing the redesign as a strategic pivot from chatbot interactions to autonomous AI agents.

Codex has reportedly grown to more than five million weekly active users, with most of them paying customers, and OpenAI wants to use ChatGPT as a gateway to push free users toward Codex and other paid products.

Two million businesses account for about 40% of OpenAI's revenue, and the company expects that share to rise to 50% by year-end, with the redesign aimed at intensifying competition with Anthropic for enterprise customers.
The redesigned interface will steer users toward coding tools, image generation and partner services such as Canva and Booking.com, according to the FT.

Thibault Sottiaux, who leads OpenAI's core product and platform teams, said the goal is 'where you have your own personal agent that is capable of helping you... across everything in your life, be it personally or at work.'

stories.headline: FDA expands Pfizer's HYMPAVZI to hemophilia A/B with inhibitors and pediatric patients aged 6–11

key_facts.fact: The FDA on June 8 approved an expanded indication for Pfizer's HYMPAVZI (marstacimab-hncq) to include treatment of patients with hemophilia A or B aged 12 and older with inhibitors and pediatric patients aged 6 to 11 with or without inhibitors.

HYMPAVZI is now indicated in the U.S. for routine prophylaxis to prevent or reduce the frequency of bleeding episodes in patients 6 years and older with hemophilia A (factor VIII deficiency) or hemophilia B (factor IX deficiency), with or without inhibitors.

The approval was supported by Phase 3 BASIS trial results in adults and adolescents 12 and older with hemophilia A or B with inhibitors, and the application received Priority Review and Breakthrough Therapy Designation from the FDA.

stories.headline: PhysicsX raises $300M Series C at $2.4B valuation to scale physics AI for jet engines and chips

key_facts.fact: London-based PhysicsX announced on June 8 that it had raised $300 million in an oversubscribed Series C at a valuation of approximately $2.4 billion, led by Singaporean sovereign wealth fund Temasek.
The $2.4 billion valuation is more than double the roughly $1 billion at which PhysicsX was valued at its Series B about a year ago.
PhysicsX builds AI models that predict how physical objects behave, replacing traditional simulation software that takes hours or days with results delivered in seconds.

CEO Jacomo Corbo said the company has a roughly six-month backlog of customer demand, that revenue will be 'close to $50 million' for the year and that the company aims to more than double that in 2027.
PhysicsX has grown from 150 to 350 employees over the past year, more than quadrupled revenue over the past two years, and will use the new capital to expand in the US and open a Singapore office.

stories.headline: Industrial AI startup PhysicsX raises $300M Series C at $2.4B led by Temasek

key_facts.fact: London-based PhysicsX raised $300 million in a Series C led by Singapore sovereign wealth fund Temasek at a valuation of roughly $2.4 billion, more than doubling the ~$1 billion valuation from its previous round 12 months earlier
New investors Intrepid Growth Partners and M&G Catalyst joined existing backers including Nvidia, Applied Materials, Atomico, General Catalyst, July Fund, NGP, Radius and Siemens

PhysicsX builds AI models that replace traditional engineering simulations, predicting physical behavior in seconds instead of hours or days; customers include Applied Materials, Siemens and Stellantis
CEO Jacomo Corbo said revenue will be 'close to US$50 million' for the year and the company aims to more than double the figure in 2027 while expanding to a roughly six-month customer backlog
PhysicsX has grown headcount from 150 to 350 over the past year and will fund US expansion plus a new Singapore office

stories.headline: Russia damages nuclear fuel storage near Chornobyl; NATO downs Russian drone over Latvia

key_facts.fact: Russia fired waves of drones and other munitions at Ukraine on Sunday June 7, with one attack damaging a nuclear fuel storage facility near the Chornobyl disaster site, Ukrainian officials said.

Early on Monday June 8, a Russian attack killed five people and injured 14 in Ukraine's southeastern Zaporizhia region, hitting infrastructure, residential buildings and cars, regional Governor Ivan Fedorov said on Telegram.
Russian attacks on energy infrastructure in the Odesa region caused power outages for more than 1,000 customers, regional Governor Oleh Kiper said.

NATO fighter jets shot down a drone that entered Latvian airspace from Russia in the early hours of June 8, the Baltic nation's army said, the latest in a series of incidents along Europe's eastern border regions; The Independent identified the interceptor as a French warplane.

Ukraine's military said it had hit oil depots in Russia-occupied Crimea, and the Institute for the Study of War assessed on June 7 that Ukrainian intermediate-range strikes are disrupting Russian ground lines of communication along the M-04 highway in occupied Luhansk and Donetsk oblasts.
A Ukrainian drone strike on the Belgorod border region killed at least one person, both sides accused each other of renewed attacks on civilians.

organizations: Institute for the Study of War

stories.headline: SpaceX flies Falcon 9 booster B1067 on record-breaking 35th mission with Starlink 10-35

key_facts.fact: SpaceX launched its Falcon 9 fleet leader, tail number B1067, on a record-breaking 35th flight from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station's Space Launch Complex 40 on Monday June 8, with the launch window opening at 6:07 a.m. EDT (10:07 UTC).
The Starlink 10-35 mission added 29 V2 mini broadband satellites to a Low Earth Orbit constellation that already includes more than 10,500 spacecraft.

As of June 7, SpaceX has seven Falcon boosters that have flown more than 25 times: B1063 (32), B1067 (34), B1069 (31), B1071 (33), B1077 (28), B1078 (28), B1080 (26), as the company pushes toward a 40-flight target per booster.

The launch came two days after SpaceX publicly disclosed it had launched two classified Starshield military satellites alongside 21 Starlink satellites on the Starlink 17-43 mission from Vandenberg pad 4E at 9:24 p.m. PDT on June 6 — a rare public acknowledgment of the government-focused satellite line.
